output:
### Summary

I read the four files in full, the diff `origin/main...HEAD`, `tests/lib.sh`, `scripts/gate.sh`, the logged gate run, and every scenario's writes into its work dir. I then ran 6 experiment sets on an archive copy of HEAD in `/tmp/bo-pt.zDzQRh` (fixture dirs only, shellcheck 0.11.0), plus read-only `gh` and primary-source lookups for the CI claims. All four acceptance criteria are met and I found no CRITICAL or HIGH defect: no real secret reaches the kept dirs, scenario names cannot traverse out of the keep dir, and the workflow interpolates no untrusted context. The findings are 2 MEDIUM and 12 LOW. The main risks are that the CI half has never run anywhere and that a keep dir placed under `tests/`, `bin/` or `lib/` turns a green gate red.

Newly added dependency: exactly one, `actions/upload-artifact@v4` (a mutable major tag, not a commit SHA; `action.yml` on that tag declares `using: node20`). `tests/run` adds no new binary (`mkdir`, `mv`, `rm` only). Already present before this change: `actions/checkout@v4`, shellcheck v0.11.0 by `curl | tar`, `tmux` by apt.

One disclosure: experiment G (`BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=-`) made `cd -` resolve to the worktree path through the inherited `OLDPWD`. The resulting `rm -rf` target contained a newline and did not exist; `git status` on the worktree is unchanged (only the two untracked `baton-runner/` dirs it started with). The scratch dir `/tmp/bo-pt.zDzQRh` is left behind; I could not remove it (the harness blocks `rm -rf` on variables).

### Findings

#### CRITICAL

None.

#### HIGH

None.

#### MEDIUM

- **Title:** The CI half of the change has never executed, and a green run cannot exercise the upload step
- **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:35-48`
- **Description:** `git branch -r --contains HEAD` prints nothing, and `gh run list` shows no run at `10d228d` (the newest runs are at `b309c27` and `85828b4`). The upload step runs only under `if: failure()`, so every green run skips it. The first time it executes will be the first red CI run, which is the moment it is needed. Three facts raise the chance it misbehaves then:
  - `actions/upload-artifact@v4` targets Node 20. The latest CI run (43778239611) carries the annotation "Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@v4". The GitHub changelog gives 2026-09-23 as the date Node 20 was removed from runners. v4 will run on a runtime it was not released for; the Node 24 line is v6.0.0 and later, and the latest release is v7.0.2.
  - The action's defaults are untested against this tree: `include-hidden-files: false`, `overwrite: false`, `if-no-files-found: warn` (v4 README and `action.yml`).
  - The step-level `env:` with `${{ runner.temp }}` is valid by the docs' context table, but it too has not run.
- **Suggested fix:** Before merge, push a throwaway commit with one failing scenario (or run `workflow_dispatch` on such a branch) and confirm the artifact holds `<name>/out` and a job's `run.log`. Move to a Node 24 release of the action (v6 or v7) pinned by commit SHA.

- **Title:** A keep dir under `tests/`, `bin/` or `lib/` flips the gate to FAIL, and it stays red after the variable is unset
- **Location:** `tests/run:17-19` with `tests/run:42` (the shellcheck glob `"$REPO"/tests/**`)
- **Description:** Reproduced on a synthetic self-suite built the way `tests/00-harness.sh:40-43` builds one, with one scenario that leaves `01-ok.sh` (`exit 0`) and `claude` (`x=1`) in its cwd:
  - no keep dir: `GATE: PASS passed=1 failed=0 shellcheck=ok`, rc 0
  - keep dir outside the repo: same PASS, rc 0
  - `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=tests/kept`: `GATE: FAIL passed=1 failed=1 shellcheck=fail`, rc 1 (SC2148 and SC2034 on the kept files)
  - next run with the variable unset, kept dir still there: still `GATE: FAIL ... shellcheck=fail`, rc 1

  On the real suite this is inferred, not run: `tests/00-harness.sh:8-9` and `:42` leave exactly such files, so the first kept run would go red. CI is unaffected because `runner.temp` is outside the checkout. The header comment does not warn about it. A keep dir elsewhere inside the repo leaves untracked files, which the spec's `receipt` row says it refuses.
- **Suggested fix:** Refuse a keep dir that resolves inside `$REPO` before any scenario runs (one `case "$KEEP/" in "$REPO"/*)` line), or say so in the header comment.

#### LOW

- **Title:** The in-flight scenario's work dir is not kept when `tests/run` is terminated, and `if: failure()` probably does not fire on a job timeout
- **Location:** `tests/run:27,34`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml:14,44`
- **Description:** The work dir is made in `TMPDIR` and moved only after the scenario ends. Reproduced: `kill -TERM` of `tests/run` during scenario 2 of 3 gave rc 143, keep dir holding only `00-first`, and 1 dir with `out` and `cwd/made` left in `TMPDIR`. A scenario that times out is kept (reproduced with `BLAST_OFF_TEST_TIMEOUT=1`: `keepL/01-hang/out` and `cwd/made` present). For the job timeout: the last CI job took 3 min 47 s; with a 300 s scenario timeout and `timeout-minutes: 30`, 6 hung scenarios pass the limit (227 + 6×300 = 2027 s > 1800 s). The docs define `failure()` as "Returns true when any previous step of a job fails" and `cancelled()` as the cancel case; they do not state the timeout case, so the "no upload on job timeout" half is not confirmed. Criterion 2 mandates `if: failure()`, so this is a gap in the criterion.
- **Suggested fix:** Make the work dir directly as `$KEEP/$name` when the variable is set (this also removes the `mv`, the nesting guard and the cross-filesystem case). Use `if: failure() || cancelled()` if hang diagnosis matters.

- **Title:** An unusable keep dir exits 1 with no `GATE:` line
- **Location:** `tests/run:18-19` against the header at `tests/run:2-3,9`
- **Description:** Reproduced with a keep path under a regular file, a keep path that is a regular file, and `-k`: each gave rc 1, only a `mkdir:` error, zero scenarios run, no verdict line. The header says the script "ends with one verdict line" and lists exit 1 as `GATE: FAIL`. It fails closed. The existing `DIR=` line at `tests/run:14` has the same shape for a missing scenario dir.
- **Suggested fix:** Print `GATE: FAIL` before exiting, or note the exception in the header.

- **Title:** The early-failure promise and the absolute-path normalisation have no test
- **Location:** `tests/run:18-19`; `tests/00-harness.sh:25-37`
- **Description:** Mutation run of lines 25-37 (copied verbatim into a scratch scenario without `lib.sh`), 9 valid mutants, 6 killed, 3 survived. Survivors:
  - dropping `KEEP="$(cd "$KEEP" && pwd)"`: the test passes, and the line is not needed since the main shell never changes directory
  - moving `mkdir -p` into the loop: the test passes, so "fails here, not after the suite ran" is unproven
  - replacing `unset BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP` with `export BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=`: the fixture's `${BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP:-}` check cannot tell unset from empty

  The test also uses only a relative keep path, while CI passes an absolute one (absolute confirmed by hand in experiment A).
- **Suggested fix:** Delete the normalisation, or add one assertion for an unmakeable keep dir (non-zero exit, no scenario output).

- **Title:** `cd "$KEEP" && pwd` breaks under an exported `CDPATH` and for the value `-`
- **Location:** `tests/run:19`
- **Description:** Reproduced. With `CDPATH` exported and a same-named dir in it, `cd` prints the path and `pwd` prints it again, so `KEEP` holds two lines; `mv` fails after the first scenario, rc 1, no verdict, 1 work dir left in `TMPDIR`, and the keep dir is empty. `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=-` does the same through `cd -` and `OLDPWD`. A leading `-` (`-k`) is read as an option by `mkdir`. `tests/run:14` has the same `CDPATH` exposure for a relative scenario dir.
- **Suggested fix:** Drop the normalisation (see the previous finding) and use `mkdir -p -- "$KEEP"`.

- **Title:** `rm -rf "$KEEP/$name"` removes any directory of that name, and stale dirs from other runs stay
- **Location:** `tests/run:34`
- **Description:** Reproduced: a pre-existing `keepK/01-ok/unrelated-user-file` was deleted without notice; `keepK/09-gone/out` (a scenario no longer in the set) and `keepK/README` survived. A keep dir reused across branches then mixes old and new evidence. In CI the dir is fresh per job (`runner.temp` is emptied per job by the docs).
- **Suggested fix:** State in the header that the dir must be dedicated to this use, or refuse a non-empty keep dir that lacks a marker file.

- **Title:** A failing `mv` or `rm` in keep mode aborts the gate with no verdict and skips the remaining scenarios
- **Location:** `tests/run:34` under `set -e` (`tests/run:10`)
- **Description:** Reproduced with a scenario leaving a `chmod 000` dir with content. Keep run 1: full verdict. Keep run 2: `rm: cannot remove ... Permission denied` after scenario 1, rc 1, no `GATE:` line, scenario 2 never ran, 1 dir left in `TMPDIR`. The unset path aborts the same way on run 1, so this is the old failure class moved one run later, not a new one. Cross-filesystem `mv` was not tested (see Validated).
- **Suggested fix:** Count the failure and continue: `... || { failed=$((failed+1)); echo "FAIL $name (work dir not kept)"; }`.

- **Title:** `mv` without `-T` and `mkdir -p` on an existing dir trust the keep dir's contents
- **Location:** `tests/run:19,34`
- **Description:** A symlink planted at `$KEEP/$name` between the `rm` and the `mv` would send the work dir into the link's target. Not reproduced as a race. What I did reproduce: a symlink already at `<keep>/01-ok` pointing at a dir with content is removed as a link, the target's `data` file is intact, and the kept dir is a real directory. This matters only for a keep dir in a shared world-writable location.
- **Suggested fix:** `mv -T`, or the make-in-place design above.

- **Title:** The new action is pinned by mutable tag
- **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:45`
- **Description:** `actions/upload-artifact@v4` can be re-pointed by its publisher. It runs after PR code, on a runner whose checkout holds a `contents: read` token (`ci.yml:9-10,16`). Same convention as the existing `actions/checkout@v4`; first-party publisher.
- **Suggested fix:** Pin both to full commit SHAs with the version in a comment.

- **Title:** Artifact scope and retention are left at defaults
- **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:44-48`
- **Description:** On any red run all 18 scenario dirs are uploaded, passed ones included, and kept for the repository default (README: "Artifacts are retained for 90 days by default"). Hidden files are dropped by default (README: "By default, hidden files are ignored by this action"), which should exclude the `.git` dirs that `tests/22-dirty-tree.sh:11`, `tests/40-receipt-required.sh:12,180` and `tests/60-preflight.sh:34-36` create; so the comment "every scenario's work dir" at `ci.yml:36` overstates. File modes are flattened to 644/755 (README). I found no hidden file under a job dir that diagnosis needs.
- **Suggested fix:** Set `retention-days` to a short value; reword the comment.

- **Title:** Static artifact name with `overwrite: false`
- **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:47`
- **Description:** The README says "If false, the action will fail if an artifact for the given name already exists." Whether a re-run attempt of the same workflow run counts as "already exists" I could not confirm from a primary source.
- **Suggested fix:** `name: blast-off-tests-${{ github.run_attempt }}`.

- **Title:** "scenarios never see it" holds for the inherited environment only
- **Location:** `tests/run:8,21`; `docs/spec.md:215`
- **Description:** Reproduced: inside a scenario the variable is unset, but `/proc/<pid>/environ` of the second ancestor (the `tests/run` bash) still shows `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=<dir>`. This is fine for the stated purpose (a nested `tests/run` must not inherit it); it is not an isolation boundary.
- **Suggested fix:** None needed; do not rely on it as isolation.

- **Title:** Already in `ci.yml` before this change: unverified shellcheck download and persisted checkout credentials
- **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:16,21`
- **Description:** The shellcheck tarball is piped from `curl` into `tar` with no checksum. `actions/checkout@v4` keeps its token in the checkout's git config by default while PR-controlled scenarios run. Neither line is part of this commit.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a `sha256sum -c` on the tarball; set `persist-credentials: false`.

### Validated

- **Confirmed correct:**
  - Criterion 1, keep: `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=<abs>` on a 2-scenario fixture gave `keepA/01-ok/{out,cwd/made}` and `keepA/02-bad/{out,cwd}`, 0 dirs left in `TMPDIR`, verdict `GATE: FAIL passed=1 failed=1 shellcheck=skipped`. Kept scenario dirs are mode 700.
  - Criterion 1, unset: empty value and unset both leave 0 dirs in `TMPDIR`; the only loop change in the diff is `tests/run:34`.
  - Criterion 2: parsed `ci.yml` with PyYAML. Step 3 has `env.BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP: ${{ runner.temp }}/blast-off-tests`; step 4 has `if: failure()` and `uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4`. The docs' context table lists `runner` for both `jobs.<job_id>.steps.env` and `steps.with`.
  - Criterion 3: `tests/run:7-8` documents the variable; `docs/spec.md:215` names the behaviour in the `00-harness` row.
  - Criterion 4: the logged gate run at this commit shows `PASS 00-harness` and `GATE: PASS passed=18 failed=0 shellcheck=ok`. My verbatim copy of lines 25-37 passes on the unmodified script (`diff` against the source lines: identical).
  - Mutants killed by lines 25-37 (6): no `unset` (verdict `passed=0 failed=2`), no removal of the earlier dir (nesting seen), `cp -r` in place of `mv`, no-op else branch, keep only `out`, keep only failed scenarios.
  - Scenario names cannot escape the keep dir: `tests/run:24,26` (glob `[0-9][0-9]-*.sh`, `basename`).
  - Keep dir that is itself a symlink works (dirs land in the target).
  - No real secret in the kept dirs: 14 of 18 scenarios pin `GH_TOKEN=dummy-not-a-token` (e.g. `tests/10-chain-done.sh:7`); `tests/lib.sh:10` unsets the Jev keys; `tests/fakes/claude:34` records `set`/`unset` only; `tests/fakes/jev:12` records 6 key characters; `lib/units.sh:19,30`, `lib/preflight.sh:29` and `lib/usage.sh:64-65` handle the token by name only. The 4 scenarios that do not pin it (00, 51, 61, 70) reach no code that writes its value.
  - No fifo or socket is created in a scenario cwd; the only symlinks point at single files (`tests/23-runner-lock.sh:26`, `tests/61-jev-pick.sh:57`).
  - Nothing consumes the artifact: `ci.yml` is the only workflow; no `download-artifact` or `workflow_run`.
  - `bash -n tests/run` passes; `shellcheck -S warning` is clean on `tests/run` and `tests/00-harness.sh`.
  - `actions/upload-artifact@v4` `action.yml`: `using: 'node20'`, `include-hidden-files: 'false'`, `overwrite: 'false'`, `if-no-files-found: 'warn'`.

- **Examined, inconclusive:**
  - `tests/run:34` across filesystems: `/tmp` and `/dev/shm` are different devices here, but the experiment rules confine me to `/tmp`, so only same-filesystem `mv` was run.
  - `ci.yml:44` on job timeout or cancel: the docs do not state what `failure()` returns then; needs a real run.
  - `ci.yml:45-48`: how the action treats symlinks, nested hidden directories and a same-name artifact on a re-run attempt; the README is silent or ambiguous; needs a real run.
  - Whether v4 works when forced onto Node 24: the annotation proves the forcing for `actions/checkout@v4`, which does work; the upload action itself has not run.
  - The shellcheck flip on the real suite: shown on a synthetic self-suite, inferred for the 18-scenario suite, which I was told not to run.
  - Size of a real 18-scenario artifact: needs a full kept run.

- **Not examined:**
  - `baton-runner/br-1115-issues/STATE.md`, `baton-phase-1-work.md` and `log.md`, changed by the same commit but outside MATERIALS.
  - Scenarios 10 to 70 at run time with a keep dir set (static read of what they write only).
  - `lib/child.sh`, `lib/chain.sh` and `bin/blast-off` beyond the token and file-name greps.
  - `actionlint` (not installed).

Sources: upload-artifact v4 README and action.yml (raw.githubusercontent.com/actions/upload-artifact/v4/), releases page (github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases), GitHub Docs "expressions" and "contexts" references, GitHub changelog 2025-09-19 "Deprecation of Node 20 on GitHub Actions runners".

### Confidence

High for the `tests/run` and test findings (each reproduced with the numbers above); medium for the workflow, which has never run. One deliberately red CI run with the artifact downloaded would settle the upload-step questions.
